turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry I'm late. The car park was rammed and I went to the wrong entrance.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's fine, sit down. Umm, bear with me, the screen's frozen again. Right. What brings you in?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Err, the receptionist said my midwife notes might not have come over. That's not actually why I'm here.
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): My husband went to a health camp at his depot last week. They were doing bloods on everyone in the canteen.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, a camp? Say that again, I was in the wrong window.
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): A screening camp. At work. They told him he's got thalasemia trait. Leaflet and everything, and I've been in bits.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. And what is it you actually want from me?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm pregnant, and I'm worried the baby could end up with the proper illness if I've got the trait as well.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): How many weeks are you?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Sixteen. No, hang on, eighteen. Midwife said eighteen on Monday and I keep getting it wrong.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any long-term illnesses? Diabetes, thyroid, anaemia?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. I am shattered though. Wiped out for two weeks... actually no, a month. I was rounding it down.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, eighteen weeks pregnant, a month of tiredness. Anything else with that? Screen just jumped.
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm irritable. Snapping at my little boy, snapping at everyone. That's new, and I hate it.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any bleeding from down below?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pain in the tummy, or tightenings?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): No. None of that.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Short of breath on the stairs?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll leave that. Any fever, feeling shivery?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): No, I haven't.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Waterworks and bowels, all alright?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): Yeah, fine.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you taking?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): Follik acid. Midwife had me on four hundred micrograms, then she changed it, no, it's five milligrams once a day, for the pregnancy.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Five milligrams once a day. Any iron, or aspirin?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Just the follik acid. I said. I'm too tired for this.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No drug allergies.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Family, then. Parents or siblings with thalasemia, sickle cell, serious anaemia? And his leaflet, alpha or beta? Sorry, I need you to repeat that, the computer ate it.

[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): Nobody in the family has it. My mum's got high blood pressure, that's separate. His leaflet says beta thalassaemia trait, haemoglobin A2 up. Left it in the car. Obviously.

[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): So nothing's confirmed on you. We simply don't know if you carry the trait, that's the open question. I'll book bloods with the nurse Thursday morning, full blood count and a haemoglobinopathy screen. No need to fast. Come before 10, and bring his leaflet if it's still on the seat.
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): Thursday. And if it comes back messy?

[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the screen is borderline we do a DNA test for the alpha genes. That one isn't booked. If you carry beta trait as well I'll refer you for genetic counselling, only then. And if you were both carriers we might talk about an amniocentesis, but only if it comes to that.
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): Fine. I just want the bloods done. I'm up at 2 googling and it's doing my head in.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll see you in two weeks with the results. Stay on the five milligrams every day, and ease off the night-time searching, it won't change Thursday's numbers.

spec.situation: Couple, wife pregnant, husband found to carry thalassaemia trait at a camp; both anxious; blood tests for the wife planned; genetic counselling discussed.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Husband having beta thalassaemia trait is stated, but not as family history.
Transcript supports no drug allergies, not all allergies.
Patient denies family thalassaemia generally; husband trait is separately stated, so scope is unclear.

omissions.text: Patient denied taking iron or aspirin; only medication is folic acid.
No drug allergies was specifically stated; recorded fact says generic 'Allergies' absent rather than medication allergies.
Patient reported occasional/questionable shortness of breath on stairs ('sometimes, not really'); this symptom was asked about and not recorded.
Patient denied feeling shivery as well as denying fever.
Family history also negative for sickle cell and serious anaemia in parents/siblings, not just thalassaemia.

Doctor said if the patient carries beta trait as well, he would refer for genetic counselling only then; the amniocentesis discussion would be if both were carriers, not specifically both beta carriers. Recorded indication says 'if both partners carry beta thalassaemia trait'.
Husband's result was described as a workplace screening result with leaflet saying beta thalassaemia trait and raised haemoglobin A2.
